report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of 3 of daedalus/spine/bootstrap.py: gate_discrimination function, ShadowResult dataclass, and start of shadow_run.
risks: gate_discrimination | high | Receipt has no integrity protection; anything that can write runs/spine/ can author a receipt. | Key management decision needed.
gate_discrimination | medium | The docstring claims 'head is resolved here, not trusted from the caller' but still accepts an explicit head parameter. | Ensure explicit head usage is intentional.
gate_discrimination | low | The revision clause uses startswith, which may match partial hashes; documented as doctrine. | Confirm that startswith is safe for the use case.

claims.text: The revision clause failed OPEN when HEAD could not be read. The test was ``if head and measured_head and not head.startswith(measured_head)``, so a falsy ``head`` skipped the staleness branch entirely. The caller in :func:`shadow_run` resolves HEAD inside a bare ``except`` that yields ``None`` — so a repository with no readable ``.git`` turned a receipt from ANY revision into ``proven=True``. ``picker._head_sha``'s own docstring said callers "fail OPEN on" None; this one's said "measured against THE CURRENT REVISION". Two documents, one code path, opposite claims. ``head`` is now resolved here when not supplied, and an unresolvable revision REFUSES.
claims.why: The code shows head is resolved here if None, and returns a refusal if not head. The revision check uses `if head and measured_head and not head.startswith(measured_head)` which now fails closed when head is None because it returns early.

claims.text: No sanity bound on the counts. ``{"planted": 12, "killed": 99}`` yielded a kill rate of 825%, which sails past an 80% floor. A rate is now rejected unless ``0 <= killed <= planted``.
claims.why: The code checks `if not (planted_f > 0 and 0 <= killed_f <= planted_f):` and returns a refusal.

claims.text: Still NOT defended, and deliberately named rather than quietly left: the receipt has no integrity protection. Anything that can write ``runs/spine/`` can author a receipt naming the current HEAD, and this function will believe it. That is a key-management decision, not a patch.
claims.why: The code does not include any cryptographic verification of the receipt; it reads and trusts the JSON content.

claims.text: Resolved HERE, not trusted from the caller, and refused when unknown. Passing an explicit head stays supported because tools/bootstrap_receipt.py deliberately asks about a DIFFERENT revision.
claims.why: The code resolves head internally if None, but still accepts an explicit head parameter.

claims.text: A receipt only counts when it is present, parseable, measured against THE CURRENT REVISION, internally consistent, clean on every critical class, and bound to the exact gate being authorised.
claims.why: The code checks each condition: existence, parseability, head match, planted/killed sanity, critical classes, and gate binding.
The code uses _gate_binding to parse expected_gate but the shape of expected_gate is not defined in this chunk; the docstring claim is about the shape.

claims.text: Callers making a promotion decision set ``require_gate_binding=True``; callers displaying the historical measurement may omit it, but that unbound answer must not be read as authority for an arbitrary candidate gate.
claims.why: The code checks `elif require_gate_binding:` and returns refusal if no expected_gate provided.

claims.text: The revision clause is the same doctrine the map and inventory sources follow: a measurement of a tree that no longer exists is not a measurement of this one.
claims.why: The claim refers to map and inventory sources not present in this chunk.

claims.text: TWO OF THESE SIX WERE PROSE UNTIL AN AUDIT FOUND THEM, and both let a forged promotion through:
claims.why: This is a historical claim about audits not verifiable from code.

claims.text: Always False while the gate is unproven. There is no override. A parameter here would be the whole design defeated by one keyword argument, which is how the containment module lost its inheritance flag as well.
claims.why: The property returns `bool(self.discrimination and self.discrimination.proven)`; it has no parameters.

claims.text: Which provider the router actually chose, read off the runner's own result rather than off the request.

Surfaced because `--local-only` DECLARES availability and does not force the choice: measured, the router still selected `claude_cli` with that lane declared unavailable, and the run stopped only because offload refuses to execute a non-free lane. Nothing was billed, but a run that ends in `no_change` for that reason looks identical to one where the model simply had no idea -- and those are completely different problems.
claims.why: This describes a scenario not present in the code chunk; refers to external behavior.

claims.text: One line a human can act on, with the caveat welded to the result.
claims.why: The verdict method returns various strings depending on state and discrimination.

observations.what: gate_discrimination returns early with refusal if head cannot be resolved, implementing fail-closed.
The receipt's planted/killed counts are sanity-checked: killed <= planted and both non-negative, planted > 0.
The revision check uses startswith, allowing partial hash matches. This is documented as doctrine.
Critical defect classes are checked before the kill rate floor, so a high kill rate with a surviving critical class is rejected.
promotion_allowed property returns False if discrimination is None or not proven; no override parameter.
routed_lane extracts 'provider' from runner_detail; returns None if not present.
verdict method handles multiple states: 'no_change' with escalation, 'no_change' without, 'gated', and other states.
The chunk ends mid-function signature for shadow_run; body not included.
